Using bayesfoRest with MetaStan

Source: vignettes/MetaStan.qmd

MetaStan fits meta-analysis models via Stan, with built-in support for binomial, normal, and Poisson likelihoods. Like brms, it supports full subgroup refitting and prior sensitivity. Subgroup analyses, prior sensitivity, and funnel plots all work.

Fit the model

Unlike brms and bayesmeta, MetaStan’s likelihood = "normal" model doesn’t take a pre-computed effect size and standard error. It wants raw two-arm data: each arm’s mean and the standard error of that mean (sd / sqrt(n)), the same way its binomial likelihood takes raw responders/sample-size per arm rather than a log odds ratio. Data has to go through create_MetaStan_dat() first, which reshapes one-row-per-study data into one-row-per-arm:

library(MetaStan)
library(bayesfoRest)

dat <- as.data.frame(cont_outcome)
dat$nd  <- 2                                          # 2 arms per study
dat$M1  <- dat$Mean_Control
dat$SE1 <- dat$SD_Control / sqrt(dat$N_Control)        # arm 1 = control
dat$M2  <- dat$Mean_Intervention
dat$SE2 <- dat$SD_Intervention / sqrt(dat$N_Intervention)  # arm 2 = intervention

metastan_dat <- create_MetaStan_dat(
  dat,
  armVars  = c(mean = "M", std.err = "SE"),
  nArmsVar = "nd")

model_metastan <- meta_stan(
  data = metastan_dat,
  likelihood = "normal",
  theta_prior = c(0, 1),        # normal(mean, variance) prior on the treatment effect
  tau_prior = 0.5,
  tau_prior_dist = "half-normal",
  chains = 4,
  iter = 4000,
  warmup = 1000)

theta_prior (not mu_prior, which is for a binomial baseline-risk term) must be specified explicitly for continuous outcomes – MetaStan errors if you leave it out.

Create the forest plot

bayes_forest() still takes the original cont_outcome data frame, not the arm-level metastan_dat – the arm reshaping is only needed to fit the model:

bayes_forest(
  model = model_metastan,
  data = cont_outcome,
  measure = "MD",
  studyvar = Author,
  yearvar = Year,
  mean_ctrl = Mean_Control,
  mean_int = Mean_Intervention,
  sd_ctrl = SD_Control,
  sd_int = SD_Intervention,
  n_ctrl = N_Control,
  n_int = N_Intervention,
  xlim = c(-8, 3)
)

Subgroup analysis and prior sensitivity

Subgroup refits work the same way as brms: subgroup = TRUE, subgroupvar = Subgroup refits MetaStan per subgroup automatically.

MetaStan also supports the full bf_*() prior-sensitivity workflow (sensitivity_plot(), ecdf_model_plot(), ecdf_prior_plot()), with one restriction: bf_student_t(), bf_half_t(), bf_exponential(), bf_lognormal()/bf_turner(), and bf_rhodes() can’t be fit exactly by MetaStan (see ?bf_priors for the full support table) – you’ll get an error rather than a silent substitution if you try. bf_normal(), bf_half_normal(), bf_half_cauchy(), and bf_uniform() all work. See vignette("brms") for a worked sensitivity example and vignette("sensitivity-analysis") for the full walkthrough.
